The KRAS gene product is a member of the small GTPase superfamily [1]. The gene is also known by the symbol KRAS [2] and the name KRAS [3], with the literature entity name Kras [4]. 

Therapeutic Targeting and Clinical Trials

KRAS has been the focus of extensive drug development efforts due to its role as the most frequently mutated oncogene [5]. Recent advances include the approval of AMG510 (sotorasib) as the first drug targeting KRAS (G12C) [5]. 

Studies have revealed that oncogenic KRAS transforms carcinoma-associated fibroblasts into lipid-laden CAFs to promote angiogenesis [6], and that KRAS-driven transcription operates predominantly through the ERK MAPK cascade [7].
